issue_context.title: "Work location" showing as an all-day event in Google Calendar
issue_context.body:
### The problem

I've just started trying to send calendar state to an LLM and have found that my "work location" field as set in my work calendar is coming through as an all-day event, so I get this: 

![Screenshot 2024-09-05 at 11 38 25](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/58b67c65-ce92-4f46-8ac8-8dc776418c4e)

I tried Googling it and found people discussing a desire to expose this information to HA in the past, but nothing about it being done or how to not show it as an event!

### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

core-2024.9.0

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

_No response_

I worried this might happen. I don't currently have a home assistant account using this feature so its a little difficult to test.

I suspect that (1) many users would like to use working location to drive automation however (2) many users don't want it showing up at all and (3) I don't want to expose lots of google calendar configuration options and want it to find a solution where it will "just work" for everyone.

Here's my best idea:
- Don't allow "working location" events to be the "next" event
- Do allow "working location" through triggers, display in the UI, and the get events services calls so they can be used in automations
- Expose "working location" as an additional sensor

The extra sensor makes the most sense to me - personally, I'd _prefer_ not to have it show up on the calendar view but equally doesn't make a big difference there, it is mainly the "next" function since that's the attribute I can get access to without having called the get_events action. If I get some time I can take a look into it but I'd hesitate to volunteer to fix it as I don't know if I'll get time or not!
Another idea could be a disabled by default working location calendar. That might solve everyone's problems.

Oh it was just to verify, I can remember you tried but it didn't work, otherwise I would've commented it.

But let's move that to a followup then
Yeah I didn't try it for this test, i'm copying the pattern of existing tests here.
Why do we let the entity decide the entity_id and why don't we let HA generate it themselves?

It's historical only, for entities created from yaml configuration. I've been assuming this would be a painful breaking change to make. My best thought was to stop doing it for this new entity type since it can use new style names with translations etc

If the entity has a unique_id you can remove it, since the used entity_id is stored in the entity registry, that's why naming changes (like the whole has_entity_name migration) is not breaking as all the entity_ids will stay consistent

OK great. Not all entities made by this integration have a unique id, but most of them do.  The ones that do not are the ones that are named based on some yaml setting. How about in a follow up PR I can stop setting the entity_id on the entity description for those cases? This change, to reduce the number of cases when entity ids are explicitly set, would still be in line with that and its still needed to set it sometimes for the yaml case.
